description: Maximally structured causal metadata: labels, levels, role, data source, physical mechanism, direct parents, direct children, Markov blanket members, CPT shape hints (which parent states most strongly drive each level), and quantitative meteorological thresholds where available. Designed to provide the richest possible prior for causal graph recovery.

variables.name: N07muVerMo
variables.label: 10.7-micron vertical motion
variables.source: GOES infrared 10.7-micron brightness-temperature tendency
variables.mechanism: IR brightness-temperature decrease over time (cooling cloud tops) indicates ascending air. Used as an objective satellite-based vertical-motion proxy, most reliable where mid-tropospheric ascent drives deep cloud.
variables.cpt_shape_hints: StrongUp most likely when SynForcng=SigPositive and QGVertMotion=StrongUp. Down most likely when SynForcng=SigNegative.
variables.quantitative_notes: Operationally, a brightness-temperature cooling rate >4°C/30 min typically maps to StrongUp.

variables.name: SubjVertMo
variables.label: Subjective vertical motion assessment
variables.source: Forecaster manual synthesis of radar, satellite, and sounding data
variables.mechanism: Expert-integrated vertical-motion judgment; synthesizes information unavailable to automated sensors. Acts as a regularizing observational node that can override purely QG-derived estimates when mesoscale features dominate.
variables.cpt_shape_hints: Highly correlated with QGVertMotion; deviates toward StrongUp when MvmtFeatures=StrongFront even if QG signal is weak.
variables.quantitative_notes: No objective threshold; purely expert categorical assessment.

variables.name: QGVertMotion
variables.label: Quasigeostrophic vertical motion
variables.source: 500 hPa height field; QG omega equation vorticity and thermal advection terms
variables.mechanism: QG omega is the primary synoptic-scale ascent diagnostic. Positive vorticity advection increasing with height plus warm-air advection both contribute upward QG forcing. This node is a direct physical driver of CombVerMo and is itself driven by large-scale WindAloft configuration.
variables.cpt_shape_hints: StrongUp probability peaks when WindAloft=NWQuad (positive-vorticity-advection maximum downstream of trough) and SynForcng=SigPositive.
variables.quantitative_notes: QG omega ≤ −5 μb/s (~−0.5 Pa/s) typically maps to StrongUp.

variables.name: CombVerMo
variables.label: Combined vertical motion
variables.source: Aggregation of N07muVerMo, SubjVertMo, QGVertMotion
variables.mechanism: Consensus lifting signal passed downstream. Serves as the primary dynamic-lifting input to both the area and instability sub-networks. Its state reflects the most probable vertical-motion regime after reconciling three independent observational channels.
variables.cpt_shape_hints: StrongUp if majority of three parents are StrongUp; Down only if all three are Down or Neutral.
variables.quantitative_notes: Effectively a majority-vote aggregation; no direct analytic formula.

variables.name: AreaMesoALS
variables.label: Area of meso-alpha-scale lifting
variables.source: Synoptic + mesoscale analysis; area extent of organized meso-alpha upward motion
variables.mechanism: Spatial extent and intensity of meso-alpha-scale (200–2000 km) organized lifting over northeastern Colorado. Strong meso-alpha lifting provides the regional backdrop that allows scattered convective cells to grow upscale into organized severe systems.
variables.cpt_shape_hints: StrongUp most likely when CombVerMo=StrongUp AND Boundaries=Strong; reduced to WeakUp when only one of the two is favorable.
variables.quantitative_notes: No direct measurable threshold; operationally assessed from composite analysis.

variables.name: SatContMoist
variables.label: Satellite moisture contribution
variables.source: GOES water-vapor channel radiances; precipitable-water satellite retrievals
variables.mechanism: Water-vapor channel (6.7 μm) diagnoses mid-tropospheric moisture. A dry 500–300 hPa layer (dark on WV imagery) indicates a dry intrusion that can both enhance lapse rates and reduce CAPE simultaneously — its net effect on hail depends on moisture depth.
variables.cpt_shape_hints: VeryWet when AreaMoDryAir=VeryWet; Dry when RHRatio=DryMMoistL and AreaMoDryAir=Dry.
variables.quantitative_notes: Precipitable water >35 mm typically maps to VeryWet; <20 mm to Dry.

variables.name: RaoContMoist
variables.label: RAO center moisture reading
variables.source: NWS/RAO surface and upper-air moisture analysis network
variables.mechanism: Operational surface/upper-air moisture analysis synthesizing surface dewpoints, rawinsondes, and model first-guess. Provides the primary ground-truth moisture estimate at the analysis time; correlates strongly with Dewpoints and LoLevMoistAd.
variables.cpt_shape_hints: VeryWet when Dewpoints=HighEverywher and LoLevMoistAd=StrongPos; Dry when Dewpoints=LowEverywhere and LoLevMoistAd=Negative.
variables.quantitative_notes: Surface dewpoints ≥60°F (15.5°C) over the plains typically indicate VeryWet; ≤45°F (7°C) indicate Dry.

variables.name: CombMoisture
variables.label: Combined moisture
variables.source: Aggregation of SatContMoist and RaoContMoist
variables.mechanism: Consensus moisture signal. Higher CombMoisture raises CAPE through elevated LCL theta-e and supports larger hailstone growth by maintaining a deep moist layer below the freezing level that reduces melting.
variables.cpt_shape_hints: VeryWet only if both parents are VeryWet or Wet; Dry if either parent is Dry and the other is Neutral.
variables.quantitative_notes: No independent measure; weighted average of the two parent signals.

variables.name: AreaMoDryAir
variables.label: Area of moisture / dry-air intrusion
variables.source: Synoptic moisture analysis; mid-level dry-air-intrusion vs. low-level moisture extent
variables.mechanism: Mid-level dry air (700–500 hPa) from the desert Southwest creates the classic 'loaded gun' sounding: steep lapse rates atop a moist BL. This node captures whether that configuration is present spatially and its areal extent, which modulates both hail size and convective mode.
variables.cpt_shape_hints: Dry (intrusion present) most likely when MidLLapse=Steep and RHRatio=DryMMoistL; VeryWet when MidLLapse=ModerateOrLe and CombMoisture=VeryWet.
variables.quantitative_notes: Mid-level RH <40% at 700–500 hPa combined with surface dewpoints >55°F is the operational 'loaded gun' threshold.

variables.name: VISCloudCov
variables.label: Visible-channel cloud cover
variables.source: GOES visible (0.65-micron) daytime imagery
variables.mechanism: Visible imagery diagnoses BL cloud fraction during daylight hours. Heavy cloud cover (Cloudy) suppresses surface heating and CAPE build-up; Clear allows maximum insolation and destabilization. PC (partly cloudy) is the transitional state most associated with convective initiation timing uncertainty.
variables.cpt_shape_hints: Cloudy when CombVerMo=StrongUp and CombMoisture=VeryWet; Clear when LowLLapse=CloseToDryAd and CombMoisture=Dry.
variables.quantitative_notes: Cloud fraction >75% → Cloudy; <25% → Clear; 25–75% → PC.

variables.name: IRCloudCover
variables.label: Infrared-channel cloud cover
variables.source: GOES IR (10.7-micron) imagery; all-hours availability
variables.mechanism: Cold cloud tops (T < −32°C, ~240 K) indicate deep convection; warm tops indicate shallow or no cloud. IR cloud cover is the all-hours complement to VIS; at night, it is the sole cloud-cover input to CombClouds.
variables.cpt_shape_hints: Cloudy with deep cold tops when CombVerMo=StrongUp; Clear when CombMoisture=Dry.
variables.quantitative_notes: Brightness temperature ≤220 K → deep convective Cloudy; ≥273 K → Clear.

variables.name: CombClouds
variables.label: Combined cloud cover
variables.source: Aggregation of VISCloudCov and IRCloudCover
variables.mechanism: Consensus cloud signal feeding BL heating diagnostics and shading effects. Cloudy inhibits daytime CAPE build-up; Clear maximizes insolation and lapse-rate steepening prior to convective initiation.
variables.cpt_shape_hints: Cloudy if either parent is Cloudy; Clear only if both are Clear.
variables.quantitative_notes: Logical union for Cloudy; intersection for Clear.

variables.name: CldShadeOth
variables.label: Non-convective cloud shading
variables.source: Cirrus, stratus, or mid-level cloud analysis; visible and IR satellite
variables.mechanism: Non-convective cloud (cirrus shields from upstream convection, advected stratus) reduces insolation independently of local convection. Can suppress CAPE even in otherwise favorable thermodynamic environments. Particularly relevant when WindAloft transports cirrus over the forecast area.
variables.cpt_shape_hints: Cloudy when WindAloft=SWQuad (advects upstream MCS anvil cirrus) and CombClouds=Cloudy.
variables.quantitative_notes: Relevant when cirrus optical depth >0.5 covers >50% of target area.

variables.name: AMInstabMt
variables.label: Morning instability over mountains
variables.source: Pre-dawn / early-morning soundings and surface obs, Front Range foothills
variables.mechanism: Elevated terrain accelerates early morning destabilization; orographic heating produces convective initiation hours before plains convection begins. Strong AM mountain instability seeds afternoon severe-storm development that propagates eastward.
variables.cpt_shape_hints: Strong when LIfr12ZDENSd=LILt_8 and AMDewptCalPl=Instability and CldShadeOth=Clear.
variables.quantitative_notes: Mountain LI <−4 and mountain-station dewpoints >50°F → Strong AM instability.

variables.name: InsInMt
variables.label: Instability over mountains
variables.source: Combined instability diagnosis, Colorado Front Range
variables.mechanism: Afternoon mountain instability; synthesizes morning instability with scenario-scaled instability to produce the net destabilization available for orographic convection. Controls outflow production and mountain-to-plains storm propagation.
variables.cpt_shape_hints: Strong when AMInstabMt=Strong and InsSclInScen=MoreUnstable and MidLLapse=Steep.
variables.quantitative_notes: Mountain CAPE >1000 J/kg → Strong; <300 J/kg → None.

variables.name: WndHodograph
variables.label: Wind hodograph shape
variables.source: Rawinsonde hodograph; directional wind shear profile surface–6 km
variables.mechanism: Hodograph shape determines storm-relative helicity (SRH) and supercell potential. DCVZFavor (Denver Cyclone / Convergence Zone hodograph) features curved, clockwise-turning shear that maximizes SRH and is the strongest discriminator of supercell-and-large-hail days in northeastern Colorado. StrongWest produces long, straight hodographs favoring squall lines with less hail.
variables.cpt_shape_hints: DCVZFavor when WindFieldPln=DenvCyclone or SEquad; StrongWest when WindAloft=NWQuad and WindFieldPln=LV.
variables.quantitative_notes: SRH (0–3 km) >150 m²/s² → DCVZFavor or curved-hodograph class; bulk shear >40 kt → StrongWest class.

variables.name: OutflowFrMt
variables.label: Outflow from mountain storms
variables.source: Surface mesonet; radar fine-line and gust-front analysis
variables.mechanism: Cold-pool outflow from afternoon mountain convection creates surface boundaries that move eastward onto the plains. Strong outflow boundaries serve as the most reliable convective trigger for severe cells forming along the mountain/plains interface.
variables.cpt_shape_hints: Strong when InsInMt=Strong and WindFieldMt=Westerly (pushes outflow eastward onto plains); None when InsInMt=None.
variables.quantitative_notes: Gust front wind shift >180° and temperature drop >8°C → Strong outflow.

variables.name: MorningBound
variables.label: Morning boundaries
variables.source: Morning surface analysis; prior-night outflow and frontal remnants
variables.mechanism: Boundaries present at sunrise — stalled fronts, remnant outflows from overnight MCS activity — provide focused low-level convergence all day. Their persistence is controlled by the synoptic flow and is particularly important on days with limited surface heating (overcast or weak insolation).
variables.cpt_shape_hints: Strong when TempDis=QStationary (stalled front overnight) and SfcWndShfDis not None.
variables.quantitative_notes: Boundary persisting >6 h after sunrise with convergence >10⁻⁴ s⁻¹ → Strong.

variables.name: Boundaries
variables.label: Active boundaries
variables.source: Synthesis of OutflowFrMt, MorningBound, and real-time surface analysis
variables.mechanism: Resultant surface convergence zone strength. The most spatially specific convective trigger in the Hailfinder network; Strong boundaries can initiate severe convection even under moderate cap and instability. Interacts multiplicatively with CapInScen and InsSclInScen in the forecast nodes.
variables.cpt_shape_hints: Strong when OutflowFrMt=Strong OR MorningBound=Strong, amplified by SfcWndShfDis=DenvCyclone or DryLine.
variables.quantitative_notes: Surface convergence >2×10⁻⁴ s⁻¹ along a coherent boundary → Strong.

variables.name: CldShadeConv
variables.label: Convective cloud shading
variables.source: Visible satellite; convective anvil and cumulus shadow analysis
variables.mechanism: Active convective anvils shade adjacent boundary layer, cooling the surface and reducing CAPE inflow into downstream cells. Marked shading can effectively terminate secondary convective development in the lee of active cells, concentrating remaining severe weather in unshaded corridors.
variables.cpt_shape_hints: Marked when CombClouds=Cloudy and CurPropConv=Strong (existing active convection); None when CurPropConv=None.
variables.quantitative_notes: Anvil shadow >50% coverage over target area → Marked.

variables.name: CompPlFcst
variables.label: Composite plains forecast tendency
variables.source: Synthesis of CapChange and InsChange over the forecast period
variables.mechanism: Summarizes the joint cap-instability trend. DecCapIncIns is the climatologically most favorable state for severe hail; IncCapDecIns strongly suppresses convection by widening the negative area on the sounding while shrinking CAPE.
variables.cpt_shape_hints: DecCapIncIns when CapChange=Decreasing and InsChange=Increasing; IncCapDecIns when CapChange=Increasing and InsChange=Decreasing.
variables.quantitative_notes: No single threshold; logical combination of parent states.

variables.name: CapChange
variables.label: Capping inversion change
variables.source: Forecast change in EML / lid strength over the plains
variables.mechanism: The EML (Elevated Mixed Layer) capping inversion prevents premature convective initiation. Its erosion (Decreasing) is necessary for severe-hail outbreaks; its strengthening (Increasing) can suppress all convection. Driven by large-scale subsidence/ascent, cloud cover, and dry-air advection.
variables.cpt_shape_hints: Decreasing when SynForcng=SigPositive and CombVerMo=StrongUp; Increasing when AreaMoDryAir=Dry and SynForcng=SigNegative.
variables.quantitative_notes: EML strength decrease >100 J/kg CIN over 6 h → Decreasing.

variables.name: LoLevMoistAd
variables.label: Low-level moisture advection
variables.source: 850 hPa wind and dewpoint analysis; southerly low-level jet
variables.mechanism: Warm, moist southerly advection at 850 hPa raises theta-e in the BL and feeds CAPE; the low-level jet (LLJ) is the primary moisture delivery mechanism into northeastern Colorado. Negative (cold/dry) advection suppresses instability development.
variables.cpt_shape_hints: StrongPos when WindFieldPln=SEquad and Dewpoints=HighEverywher; Negative when WindFieldPln=LV or LongAnticyc.
variables.quantitative_notes: 850 hPa theta-e advection >4 K/3h → StrongPos; <−2 K/3h → Negative.

variables.name: InsChange
variables.label: Instability change
variables.source: Forecast change in CAPE and lapse rates over the forecast period
variables.mechanism: Rising CAPE (Increasing) results from combination of BL moisture increase, solar heating, and lapse-rate steepening. Increasing instability paired with Decreasing cap is the necessary condition for severe convective outbreak. The interaction between InsChange and CapChange is the central nonlinear threshold in the Hailfinder network.
variables.cpt_shape_hints: Increasing when CombMoisture=VeryWet and LoLevMoistAd=StrongPos and CldShadeConv=None; Decreasing when CldShadeConv=Marked.
variables.quantitative_notes: CAPE increase >500 J/kg over forecast period → Increasing.

variables.name: MountainFcst
variables.label: Mountain region (R1) severe-weather forecast
variables.source: Final probabilistic hail-severity forecast, Colorado Front Range / mountain region
variables.mechanism: Terminal node. SVR indicates high probability of severe hail (diameter ≥3/4 inch) over the mountain region. Driven principally by mountain instability, boundary focusing, and scenario-scaled capping. Conditionally independent of plains nodes given its direct parents.
variables.cpt_shape_hints: SVR when InsInMt=Strong, Boundaries=Strong, WndHodograph=DCVZFavor, CapInScen=LessThanAve.
variables.quantitative_notes: Operationally: CAPE >1500 J/kg + SRH >200 m²/s² + no cap → SVR.

variables.name: Date
variables.label: Seasonal date bucket
variables.source: Calendar date grouped into phenological hail-season windows
variables.mechanism: Root node (no parents in the network). Encodes seasonal climatological priors: jet stream position, moisture-regime frequency, and synoptic-pattern prevalence all shift substantially across the six windows. Peak northeastern Colorado severe-hail frequency is Jun15–Jul15.
variables.cpt_shape_hints: Jun15_Jul1 and Jul2_Jul15 → highest prior probability of Scenario classes associated with severe hail (D, G, H).
variables.quantitative_notes: Climatological hail-day frequency peaks at ~0.25/day during Jun15–Jul15 in northeastern Colorado.

variables.name: Scenario
variables.label: Synoptic-scale weather scenario
variables.source: Expert-defined synoptic pattern classification A–K; upper-air and surface composite analysis
variables.mechanism: Root contextual node (only Date as parent). Encodes the dominant large-scale synoptic archetype for the day. Each scenario carries distinct climatological priors for CIN, instability, moisture, and wind shear that propagate through every scenario-relative normalization node in the network.
variables.cpt_shape_hints: Scenarios D, G, H most probable during peak season with strong southwesterly flow; scenarios A, B associated with quiescent synoptic pattern.
variables.quantitative_notes: Scenario classification based on 500 hPa height pattern and surface synoptic type; 11 archetypes cover the full northeastern Colorado severe-hail climatology.

variables.name: ScenRelAMCIN
variables.label: Scenario grouping for AM CIN
variables.source: Partitions Scenario into two groups based on expected morning CIN behavior
variables.mechanism: Scenarios A–B are characterized by weak or absent morning CIN (weak synoptic pattern, good mixing); scenarios C–K span a wide range but generally have more significant morning inhibition from EML or subsidence. This binary partition is used to set conditional probability tables for MorningCIN.
variables.cpt_shape_hints: AB → MorningCIN=None more probable; CThruK → PartInhibit or Stifling more probable.
variables.quantitative_notes: Scenarios A, B: median morning CIN < 25 J/kg; C–K: median 50–200 J/kg.

variables.name: MorningCIN
variables.label: Morning convective inhibition
variables.source: Sunrise rawinsonde or surface-based CIN estimate from 12Z Denver sounding
variables.mechanism: Observed CIN at forecast start. Stifling (CIN ~100–250 J/kg) requires extraordinary forcing to overcome; TotalInhibit (>250 J/kg) essentially precludes surface-based convection. Interaction with CapChange determines whether cap will erode by afternoon.
variables.cpt_shape_hints: None when ScenRelAMCIN=AB and CapChange=Decreasing; TotalInhibit when ScenRelAMCIN=CThruK and CapChange=Increasing.
variables.quantitative_notes: CIN 0–25 J/kg → None; 25–100 → PartInhibit; 100–250 → Stifling; >250 → TotalInhibit.

variables.name: AMCINInScen
variables.label: AM CIN relative to scenario baseline
variables.source: Normalizes MorningCIN against scenario-specific climatological CIN
variables.mechanism: Anomaly encoding that accounts for the fact that the same absolute CIN value means very different things across scenarios. MoreThanAve CIN suppresses convection even in otherwise favorable synoptic archetypes (scenarios G, H) where average CIN is already low.
variables.cpt_shape_hints: LessThanAve when MorningCIN=None in ScenRelAMCIN=CThruK context; MoreThanAve when MorningCIN=Stifling in any scenario.
variables.quantitative_notes: Computed as (observed CIN − scenario median CIN) / scenario IQR.

variables.name: CapInScen
variables.label: Capping relative to scenario baseline
variables.source: Afternoon capping strength normalized to scenario climatology
variables.mechanism: Anomalous cap weakness (LessThanAve) within a given scenario is the key probabilistic lever that elevates SVR probability in all forecast nodes simultaneously. Acts as a d-separation gate: once CapInScen is observed, Scenario and MorningCIN become conditionally independent of the forecast nodes given this node.
variables.cpt_shape_hints: LessThanAve when AMCINInScen=LessThanAve and CapChange=Decreasing; MoreThanAve when AMCINInScen=MoreThanAve and CapChange=Increasing.
variables.quantitative_notes: Same normalization formula as AMCINInScen but applied to afternoon CIN re-assessment.

variables.name: ScenRelAMIns
variables.label: Scenario grouping for AM instability
variables.source: Partitions Scenario into six instability-regime groups
variables.mechanism: Six instability regime groups with distinct prior distributions for morning LI and CAPE. Group G (strong southwesterly flow + deep moisture) and H (pre-frontal environment) have the highest prior probability of Strong AM instability; ABI is most benign.
variables.cpt_shape_hints: G and H groups → LIfr12ZDENSd=LILt_8 elevated probability; ABI → LIGt0 most probable.
variables.quantitative_notes: Group G has climatological median 12Z LI of −4; ABI median LI of +2.

variables.name: LIfr12ZDENSd
variables.label: Lifted index — 12Z Denver sounding
variables.source: 12Z rawinsonde launch, Denver (KDVN / KDEN); surface-parcel lifted index
variables.mechanism: Most direct instability observation in the network. LI is the temperature of the environment minus the temperature of a surface parcel lifted to 500 hPa; negative values indicate instability. LILt_8 (LI ≤ −8) corresponds to extreme CAPE (>3000 J/kg) and is a strong discriminator for very large hail.
variables.cpt_shape_hints: LILt_8 when MidLLapse=Steep and AMDewptCalPl=Instability and LowLLapse=CloseToDryAd; LIGt0 when LowLLapse=Stable.
variables.quantitative_notes: LI > 0 → LIGt0; −4 < LI ≤ 0 → N1GtLIGt_4 (CAPE ~300–1000 J/kg); −8 < LI ≤ −5 → N5GtLIGt_8 (CAPE ~1500–3000 J/kg); LI ≤ −8 → LILt_8 (CAPE >3000 J/kg).

variables.name: AMDewptCalPl
variables.label: AM dewpoint calculation — plains
variables.source: Morning surface dewpoint network, northeastern Colorado plains mesonet
variables.mechanism: Surface dewpoint is the most direct BL moisture proxy; controls theta-e and hence CAPE. High plains dewpoints (Instability state) produce surface-based CAPE of 1000–3000+ J/kg in combination with steep mid-level lapse rates.
variables.cpt_shape_hints: Instability when Dewpoints=HighEverywher or LowMtsHighPl and LoLevMoistAd=StrongPos; Stability when Dewpoints=LowEverywhere.
variables.quantitative_notes: Plains surface Td ≥60°F (15.5°C) → Instability; 50–59°F → Neutral; <50°F → Stability.

variables.name: AMInsWliScen
variables.label: AM instability relative to scenario
variables.source: Normalizes morning instability (LI / dewpoint) against scenario-specific baseline
variables.mechanism: Scenario-relative instability anomaly. MoreUnstable within scenario G or H (already high baseline) represents extreme CAPE environments. Interaction with CapInScen is the key multiplicative term: high instability anomaly plus low cap anomaly → nearly certain SVR.
variables.cpt_shape_hints: MoreUnstable when LIfr12ZDENSd=LILt_8 and AMDewptCalPl=Instability regardless of scenario; LessUnstable when LIfr12ZDENSd=LIGt0.
variables.quantitative_notes: Computed as (observed LI − scenario-median LI) / scenario IQR.

variables.name: InsSclInScen
variables.label: Instability scaling within scenario
variables.source: Final scenario-scaled instability, combining AM and afternoon instability signals
variables.mechanism: Calibrated instability input to all three regional forecast terminal nodes. Accounts for scenario-specific thermodynamic baseline before propagating instability signal. Acts as an information bottleneck: downstream forecast nodes depend on instability only through this node and CapInScen.
variables.cpt_shape_hints: MoreUnstable when AMInsWliScen=MoreUnstable and InsChange=Increasing; LessUnstable when both are on the low end.
variables.quantitative_notes: No independent analytic threshold; effectively a propagation of AMInsWliScen updated by InsChange direction.

variables.name: ScenRel34
variables.label: Scenario grouping for regions 2/3/4
variables.source: Partitions Scenario into five groups for northeastern Colorado plains sub-regions
variables.mechanism: Geographic sub-regionalization: different scenario groups produce distinct spatial hail-climatology fingerprints across sub-regions 2–4. Group HI scenarios are most strongly associated with widespread plains severe hail in sub-regions 2–4.
variables.cpt_shape_hints: HI scenario group → elevated SVR prior for N34StarFcst; ACEFK → XNIL more probable.
variables.quantitative_notes: Climatological SVR frequency: HI group ~30%; ACEFK ~5% for regions 2–4.

variables.name: LatestCIN
variables.label: Latest convective inhibition estimate
variables.source: Afternoon mesoanalysis or sounding-based CIN update near forecast valid time
variables.mechanism: Updated CIN at or near valid time. Most proximate CIN information to the forecast; represents the actual inhibition state that convection must overcome. Stifling/TotalInhibit sharply reduces CurPropConv regardless of instability or forcing.
variables.cpt_shape_hints: None when MorningCIN=None and CapChange=Decreasing; TotalInhibit when MorningCIN=TotalInhibit and CapChange=Increasing.
variables.quantitative_notes: Uses same thresholds as MorningCIN but evaluated at forecast valid time (typically 18–21Z).

variables.name: LLIW
variables.label: LLIW severe-weather composite index
variables.source: Low-Level Index of Wind shear; composite of low-level shear, BL moisture, instability
variables.mechanism: Combines low-level wind shear (0–1 km SRH), BL moisture (theta-e), and instability (CAPE) into a single index. Strong LLIW is strongly correlated with supercell and large-hail environments; it is one of the most discriminating predictors in the Hailfinder network for SVR vs. SIG distinction.
variables.cpt_shape_hints: Strong when WndHodograph=DCVZFavor and CombMoisture=VeryWet and InsSclInScen=MoreUnstable.
variables.quantitative_notes: LLIW strong threshold corresponds approximately to SRH >300 m²/s² + CAPE >2000 J/kg + Td >60°F.

variables.name: CurPropConv
variables.label: Current propensity to convection
variables.source: Real-time synthesis of LatestCIN, LLIW, boundaries, and hodograph
variables.mechanism: Immediate probabilistic assessment integrating the cap state (LatestCIN), forcing index (LLIW), boundary focusing (Boundaries), and shear (WndHodograph). Acts as the primary pre-terminal aggregation node: Strong CurPropConv with anomalously low cap is the near-sufficient condition for SVR in all three regional forecast nodes.
variables.cpt_shape_hints: Strong when LatestCIN=None, LLIW=Strong, Boundaries=Strong, WndHodograph=DCVZFavor; None when LatestCIN=TotalInhibit regardless of other parents.
variables.quantitative_notes: LatestCIN=TotalInhibit → P(None) > 0.95 regardless of LLIW.

variables.name: ScnRelPlFcst
variables.label: Scenario pass-through for plains forecast
variables.source: Direct pass-through of Scenario to plains forecast sub-network
variables.mechanism: Structural copy of Scenario that preserves scenario-specific CPT calibration for the PlainsFcst node. Ensures that the scenario prior is incorporated into plains forecast independently of the instability and cap sub-network paths, preventing d-separation artifacts in inference.
variables.cpt_shape_hints: Functionally identical to Scenario; CPT for PlainsFcst given ScnRelPlFcst mirrors scenario-specific hail climatology.
variables.quantitative_notes: Deterministic function of Scenario; P(ScnRelPlFcst=X | Scenario=X) = 1.

variables.name: PlainsFcst
variables.label: Plains severe-weather forecast
variables.source: Final hail-severity forecast, northeastern Colorado plains
variables.mechanism: Terminal forecast node. SVR = high probability of severe hail (diameter ≥3/4 inch) over plains. Integration node for all upstream paths: instability (InsSclInScen), cap (CapInScen), forcing tendency (CompPlFcst), initiation (CurPropConv + Boundaries), and scenario climatology (ScnRelPlFcst). XNIL = no significant hail expected; SIG = hail likely but below severe threshold.
variables.cpt_shape_hints: SVR when CompPlFcst=DecCapIncIns and CapInScen=LessThanAve and CurPropConv=Strong; XNIL when LatestCIN=TotalInhibit propagated through CurPropConv.
variables.quantitative_notes: SVR historically corresponds to POD ~0.75, FAR ~0.35 in the original Abramson et al. (1996) evaluation.

variables.name: N34StarFcst
variables.label: Regions 2/3/4 severe-weather forecast
variables.source: Final hail-severity forecast, NE Colorado sub-regions 2–4
variables.mechanism: Terminal forecast node for sub-regions 2–4 east of the primary plains corridor. Shares most upstream drivers with PlainsFcst but additionally conditioned on ScenRel34 (regional scenario climatology) and AreaMesoALS (large-scale lifting area extent necessary for convection to reach these distal regions).
variables.cpt_shape_hints: SVR requires both CurPropConv=Strong AND AreaMesoALS=StrongUp, reflecting need for organized large-scale lift to sustain severe convection in distal sub-regions.
variables.quantitative_notes: Sub-regions 2–4 have ~30% lower baseline SVR frequency than the primary plains region.

variables.name: R5Fcst
variables.label: Region 5 severe-weather forecast
variables.source: Final hail-severity forecast, eastern plains edge (Region 5)
variables.mechanism: Terminal forecast node for the far-eastern fringe of the domain. At this distance from the orographic trigger, SVR requires either strong synoptic forcing to sustain convection or propagating organized systems. Primarily driven by CurPropConv and SynForcng; less dependent on local boundary effects.
variables.cpt_shape_hints: SVR requires CurPropConv=Strong and SynForcng=SigPositive; Boundaries alone insufficient without synoptic support at this distance.
variables.quantitative_notes: Region 5 SVR frequency roughly half that of plains core region in the northeastern Colorado hail climatology.

variables.name: Dewpoints
variables.label: Spatial dewpoint pattern
variables.source: Surface mesonet dewpoint network, northeastern Colorado plains and foothills
variables.mechanism: Spatial gradient of surface dewpoints defines theta-e ridges, moisture-convergence corridors, and the dryline position. HighEverywher represents the most favorable BL moisture state; LowMtsHighPl indicates plains moisture pool with dry mountains, supporting enhanced instability contrast.
variables.cpt_shape_hints: HighEverywher when LoLevMoistAd=StrongPos and WindFieldPln=SEquad; LowEverywhere when LoLevMoistAd=Negative.
variables.quantitative_notes: Plains area-mean Td ≥62°F → HighEverywher; ≤48°F → LowEverywhere.

variables.name: LowLLapse
variables.label: Low-level lapse rate
variables.source: Surface–850 hPa temperature gradient; Denver sounding or mesoanalysis
variables.mechanism: Near-surface lapse rate controls BL mixing depth and sensible-heat flux contribution to CAPE. CloseToDryAd (superadiabatic) indicates deep, vigorous mixing layer; Stable indicates inversion or cold air advection suppressing BL development.
variables.cpt_shape_hints: CloseToDryAd when CldShadeOth=Clear and SynForcng in {SigPositive,NegToPos}; Stable when SynForcng=SigNegative.
variables.quantitative_notes: Surface–850 hPa lapse rate ≥9.8°C/km → CloseToDryAd; 7–9°C/km → Steep; 4–7°C/km → ModerateOrLe; <4°C/km → Stable.

variables.name: MeanRH
variables.label: Mean relative humidity
variables.source: Surface–500 hPa layer-mean RH from sounding or model analysis
variables.mechanism: Layer-mean RH controls both CAPE (higher RH → higher theta-e) and hail-melting rate below the freezing level (VeryMoist reduces melting, supporting larger hail at the surface). Dry mid-levels paired with moist BL (the DryMMoistL RHRatio state) is the optimal hail-growth configuration.
variables.cpt_shape_hints: VeryMoist when CombMoisture=VeryWet and AreaMoDryAir=VeryWet; Dry when AreaMoDryAir=Dry and SynForcng=SigNegative.
variables.quantitative_notes: Layer-mean RH > 70% → VeryMoist; 40–70% → Average; <40% → Dry.

variables.name: MidLLapse
variables.label: Mid-level lapse rate
variables.source: 700–500 hPa temperature gradient; Denver 12Z rawinsonde
variables.mechanism: The 700–500 hPa lapse rate is the signature of the EML (Elevated Mixed Layer) from the Southwest desert; values ≥8°C/km create large CAPE and a deep hail-growth zone. Steep mid-level lapse rates are one of the two most discriminating large-hail predictors in northeastern Colorado (the other being low-level moisture).
variables.cpt_shape_hints: Steep when WindAloft=SWQuad or NWQuad and AreaMoDryAir=Dry (EML advection from SW desert); ModerateOrLe when AreaMoDryAir=VeryWet.
variables.quantitative_notes: 700–500 hPa lapse rate ≥8.5°C/km → CloseToDryAd; 7–8.5°C/km → Steep; <7°C/km → ModerateOrLe.

variables.name: MvmtFeatures
variables.label: Movement of synoptic features
variables.source: Short-range forecast / observed motion of fronts, upper troughs, jet streaks
variables.mechanism: Rapidly moving synoptic features import fresh forcing and renew QG ascent. StrongFront can generate mesoscale lift that overcomes even substantial CIN; MarkedUpper (fast-moving upper trough) provides rapid QG forcing without necessarily creating a surface boundary.
variables.cpt_shape_hints: StrongFront when SynForcng=NegToPos and surface analysis shows <12 h frontal passage; MarkedUpper when WindAloft=NWQuad and upper trough moving >30 kt.
variables.quantitative_notes: Feature movement >30 kt → StrongFront or MarkedUpper; <10 kt → NoMajor.

variables.name: RHRatio
variables.label: Mid- to low-level RH ratio
variables.source: Ratio of mid-level (700–500 hPa) to low-level (surface–850 hPa) relative humidity
variables.mechanism: DryMMoistL (dry mid-levels over moist BL) is the quintessential large-hail sounding configuration for northeastern Colorado: steep EML lapse rates create large CAPE while dry mid-levels maintain a warm, dry hail-growth zone that maximizes hailstone size and minimizes melting. MoistMDryL suppresses CAPE despite surface moisture.
variables.cpt_shape_hints: DryMMoistL when MidLLapse=Steep and AreaMoDryAir=Dry and LowLLapse=CloseToDryAd; MoistMDryL when MeanRH=VeryMoist throughout.
variables.quantitative_notes: Mid-level RH <45% with low-level RH >70% → DryMMoistL; mid-level RH >65% with low-level RH <50% → MoistMDryL.

variables.name: SfcWndShfDis
variables.label: Surface wind shifts and discontinuities
variables.source: Surface mesonet; radar fine-line analysis; boundary-layer convergence zone mapping
variables.mechanism: Surface boundaries and wind-shift lines provide the most reliable convective trigger in the region. The Denver Cyclone (DenvCyclone) is a mesoscale circulation unique to the Denver area driven by differential terrain heating; it generates convergence, hodograph curvature, and anomalously high SRH. Dryline provides sharp moisture-convergence focusing. E_W_N and E_W_S reflect east-west-oriented wind-shift lines with different moisture-advection geometry.
variables.cpt_shape_hints: DenvCyclone when WindFieldPln=DenvCyclone; DryLine when WindFieldPln=SEquad and Dewpoints shows sharp east-west gradient.
variables.quantitative_notes: Denver Cyclone identifiable by surface wind rotation >180° in <50 km radius centered near Denver.

variables.name: SynForcng
variables.label: Synoptic forcing tendency
variables.source: QG forcing / upper divergence / jet-streak analysis; large-scale lift diagnostics
variables.mechanism: Large-scale dynamic forcing driver that propagates influence to virtually every other node in the network. SigPositive forcing can overcome 100–200 J/kg CIN and is necessary for widespread SVR events. SigNegative (strong subsidence/negative-vorticity-advection regime) effectively vetoes convection regardless of thermodynamic state.
variables.cpt_shape_hints: SigPositive when WindAloft=NWQuad (downstream of upper trough, max divergence); SigNegative when WindAloft=SWQuad (upstream of ridge, max convergence).
variables.quantitative_notes: Upper-level divergence >4×10⁻⁵ s⁻¹ → SigPositive; <−2×10⁻⁵ s⁻¹ → SigNegative.

variables.name: TempDis
variables.label: Temperature discontinuities
variables.source: Surface analysis / mesonet; frontal thermal-boundary analysis
variables.mechanism: Thermal boundaries generate differential heating gradients and local wind-shear enhancement. QStationary boundaries are particularly potent because they persist over the target area for extended periods, allowing BL heating on the warm side while maintaining convergence. Moving boundaries can trigger convection over a larger swath.
variables.cpt_shape_hints: QStationary when MvmtFeatures=NoMajor and SynForcng=LittleChange; Moving when MvmtFeatures=StrongFront.
variables.quantitative_notes: Frontal motion <5 kt → QStationary; >20 kt → Moving.

variables.name: WindAloft
variables.label: Upper-level wind field
variables.source: 300–200 hPa wind analysis; jet stream position and quadrant relative to forecast area
variables.mechanism: Jet stream quadrant position determines the sign and magnitude of upper-level divergence over the forecast area. NWQuad (entrance region of jet from the northwest) provides maximum left-exit divergence → strongest synoptic ascent. SWQuad (right-entrance region) produces convergence and suppresses convection.
variables.cpt_shape_hints: NWQuad most probable in scenarios D, G, H during peak season; SWQuad in scenarios A, B.
variables.quantitative_notes: Jet-core wind ≥70 kt at 300 hPa with NW flow → NWQuad; <30 kt → LV (light and variable).

variables.name: WindFieldMt
variables.label: Wind field over mountains
variables.source: 700 hPa analysis and mountain-station surface winds (Stapleton, Grand Junction)
variables.mechanism: Westerly 700 hPa flow drives orographic lifting over the Front Range, promoting afternoon mountain convection initiation. LVorOther (light/variable or non-westerly) reduces orographic forcing and delays or prevents mountain storm initiation, hence reducing outflow production onto the plains.
variables.cpt_shape_hints: Westerly when WindAloft in {SWQuad, NWQuad}; LVorOther when WindAloft=LV.
variables.quantitative_notes: 700 hPa westerly component ≥15 kt → Westerly; <5 kt → LVorOther.

variables.name: WindFieldPln
variables.label: Wind field over plains
variables.source: Surface and 850 hPa wind analysis, northeastern Colorado plains mesonet
variables.mechanism: BL flow regime controls moisture-flux direction, boundary formation, and hodograph shape over the plains. DenvCyclone and SEquad (southeasterly) are most strongly linked to severe hail: DenvCyclone via hodograph curvature and convergence focus; SEquad via maximum low-level moisture advection from the Gulf. LongAnticyc (longwave anticyclonic) typically suppresses convection via subsidence and dry advection.
variables.cpt_shape_hints: DenvCyclone when SynForcng=SigPositive and WindAloft=NWQuad; SEquad when WindAloft=SWQuad and TempDis=Moving; LongAnticyc when SynForcng=SigNegative.
variables.quantitative_notes: 850 hPa southeasterly flow ≥15 kt → SEquad; surface cyclonic curvature centered near Denver with ≤10 kt speed → DenvCyclone.
